findings.evidence: Request count is not severity or willingness to pay; a few loud users can file most tickets. Weigh requests against observed behavior.
findings.fix: Replace this widely known product-management point with a fact the model would miss, such as how to read this repo's ticket labels or telemetry event names. If no such fact exists, drop the bullet. Keep the code-is-not-availability and stale-roadmap gotchas.

findings.evidence: Before writing, confirm every citation resolves: the file and line exist, the issue number exists, the metric or query name is real.
findings.fix: Shorten this to one clause, e.g. 'Drop or relabel as hypothesis any citation you did not open.' Checking that a citation exists is generic, and the model already knows to do it.

findings.evidence: For each, check once: whether the idea removes the binding step or unlocks the group, or only relieves the symptom; its value mechanism (...); and a segment-and-metric hypothesis with its cheapest test.
findings.fix: Split the Discover check into a short numbered sub-list: (a) binding step or symptom, (b) value mechanism, (c) segment, metric and cheapest test. Each check should be a separate gate the agent fills in per idea, not three checks packed into one sentence.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list covers trend features, anchoring on the request, made-up reach and parity features, but not citing evidence the agent never opened
findings.fix: Add: 'NEVER cite a file, issue or metric you did not open in this session: a fabricated citation in a saved decision record gets carried forward by every later session as fact.'

findings.evidence: Description has no retention or churn keywords and no 'even without the word 10x' clause, yet trigger queries such as 'churn is killing us, where do we focus our two devs' depend on them
findings.fix: Find and rank high-leverage product opportunities from repository, feedback and usage evidence, saved as a strategy session file. Use when users ask what to build next or where to focus a small team, want a product to be substantially more valuable, stickier or less churn-prone, ask for '10x' ideas, growth levers, product bets or small wins, or ask whether a requested feature is the right next move, even if they never say '10x' or 'strategy'. Gives recommendations and assumptions to validate only; not for implementing code, sprint plans, user stories, effort estimates, competitor or pricing research, or committed-date roadmaps.

findings.evidence: | Rank | Idea | Priority | Evidence or hypothesis | Value mechanism | Reach (...) | Adoption cost (...) | Effort (...) | Risk (...) | Deciding trade-off | Assumption to validate |
findings.fix: Make the 11-column table the default only for evidence-backed sessions. When there is no evidence or the request is a single feature, allow a compact form (Idea, Priority, Mechanism, Effort, Assumption to validate) and state which fields were omitted and why.

findings.evidence: Negatives such as 'brainstorm names for our new mobile app', 'fix a button alignment bug in our product' and 'design a database schema for team collaboration' share almost no intent with the skill
findings.fix: Replace two or three of these with near-misses, e.g. 'summarize our NPS survey themes for the all-hands, no recommendations' or 'write a PRD for the approved shared-challenges feature'.

findings.evidence: For one requested feature (such as "add CSV export"), check the Baseline first ... compare it with at least one broader opportunity on impact and feasibility before recommending.
findings.fix: State whether the single-feature path still writes a full session file with five to ten ideas, or a shorter comparison with one Do Now. The step 4 default ('five to ten ideas') and this path currently disagree.

findings.evidence: Every Reach cell names the user-base number from the request or evidence, in the template's form.
findings.fix: Add a fallback for when neither the request nor the evidence gives a user-base number: 'If no user-base number exists, write "unknown base; measure active users of <flow>" and add it as a validation question.'
